_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.

themes.title: Section 338 Canada tariffs — Aug 21 EOD hard binary (tariff effective Aug 22 if no deal), Trump says 'very good deal,' Carney cautious, deal framework emerging
themes.summary: As of August 20, the Section 338 binary has evolved materially. Hours before the original 12:01am ET August 19 deadline, President Trump paused the 50% tariff for three days, citing a tentative deal. Trump described it to reporters as a 'very good deal for both parties' and mentioned the Keystone XL pipeline 'may be awoken from the grave.' Prime Minister Carney's statement was deliberately more cautious — he confirmed the tariff was postponed 'until end of day, August 21' and reiterated that 'substantial progress has been made, although there is important work still to be done.' Carney's statement conspicuously did not mention a deal or a pipeline. The divergence between Trump's 'deal struck' framing and Carney's 'progress made' framing is the key interpretive tension entering the Aug 21 deadline. Quebec Premier Christine Frechette, entering the legislature the morning of Aug 19, said she had not seen all the terms and reiterated her red line: supply management on dairy and protection of culture and language. On the deal mechanics, the Globe and Mail reports that the framework under negotiation would see the US lower — but not eliminate — some Section 232 tariffs in exchange for Canadian concessions including provinces lifting their US alcohol bans and Ottawa dropping its counter-tariffs on autos; Canadian premiers have conditioned the alcohol concession on meaningful tariff changes. Per GHY International and CBP mechanics, the operative new hard deadline for shippers and FX markets is August 22 at 12:01am ET — a shipment that crosses on August 21 but is entered for consumption after midnight August 22 attracts the 50% levy. The statutory mechanics remain unchanged: 50% additional ad valorem tariff on approximately $20 billion of Canadian goods (motor vehicles, dairy, alcoholic beverages, cement, furniture, clothing, and others), stacking on top of all existing duties with no USMCA/CUSMA exemption. Energy, potash, fish, critical minerals, and Section 232-covered goods remain excluded. Three scenarios remain live entering August 21: (1) Deal announced by Aug 21 EOD — now the elevated-probability path given 'deal' language from Trump and intensifying negotiator optimism per Globe and Mail sources; (2) Further extension/delay — lower-probability given the explicit Aug 21 language and Trump's framing of an agreement; (3) Tariffs land Aug 22 — tail risk, but Carney's caution and unresolved provincial supply-management red lines keep this scenario non-trivial.

implications.CAD: RELIEF partially priced on Aug 19 open given Trump's 'deal' framing — USDCAD should have compressed toward 1.3850-1.3900 range on the open. The Aug 21 EOD binary (effective Aug 22 tariff) still dominates: (1) Deal confirmed by Aug 21 = sharp CAD relief, 100-150 pips from pre-Aug 19 levels, theme retires — now elevated-probability path given Trump's language and negotiator optimism; (2) Further delay = 30-50 pip CAD relief, theme extends; (3) Tariffs land Aug 22 = USDCAD gaps higher 100-150 pips, Canada retaliation cliff materialises. Do not carry unhedged CAD into Aug 21 close. Provincial supply-management and alcohol concessions remain the sticking points that could prevent a clean deal by Aug 21.
implications.USD: USDCAD directional narrative is dominated by the Aug 21 binary. Broad USD softness from data miss trifecta (NFP + CPI + PPI) and Jackson Hole positioning is a secondary counterweight. Post-Aug 21 resolution (either direction), Fed/Jackson Hole theme reasserts as the primary USD driver.
implications.MXN: Secondary exposure — USDMXN can telegraph risk sentiment around Canada shock in real time. US-Mexico USMCA track advancing more smoothly per prior reporting.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD may be volatile around Aug 21 resolution. EU under separate tariff ceiling; EU-Canada trade linkage adds modest contagion risk to EUR crosses in a CAD shock scenario.
implications.AUD: Indirect risk-off commodity bloc contagion if CAD volatility spills broadly on Aug 21. AUDCAD may spike on the binary outcome.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol spike risk around Aug 21 close.

themes.title: Japan-US joint FX intervention regime — USDJPY 158.53 on Aug 20, BOJ Sep hike ~80% priced, Japan national CPI Aug 21 is the immediate hard catalyst
themes.summary: As of August 20, USDJPY is trading at 158.53, up 0.23% on the day, continuing to consolidate in the 158.50-159.50 range. The intervention regime remains in a consolidation phase — no follow-up intervention has landed since the initial joint US-Japan action in late July/early August (approximate low of ~155.20 on August 3), a gap of over two and a half weeks that continues to allow carry traders to rebuild short-JPY positions. The pair is roughly 2.8% below the 2026 high of 163.85 set on July 28, reflecting the intervention-led technical break that has not been fully repaired. The BOJ September hike case has continued to solidify. Reuters, citing three sources familiar with BOJ thinking (August 14), reports the BOJ is set to raise rates as soon as September and is likely to hike more aggressively thereafter from the current pace of roughly twice a year. MUFG Research (August 17) marks market pricing at approximately 80% probability of a BOJ hike in September, up from ~65% on August 7. MUFG's baseline projects the BOJ to raise to 1.25% in September 2026, 1.50% in January 2027, and 1.75% in June 2027. The BOJ's June meeting minutes (released August 10) showed most board members judged higher crude oil costs were broadly filtering through to consumer prices, with several warning underlying inflation could overshoot 2% and two members favouring faster rate hikes. At the July meeting (8-1, Takata dissented for immediate hike to 1.25%), the BOJ kept rates at 1.0% and warned underlying inflation could exceed 2%. The immediate catalyst is Japan national CPI, releasing August 21 — the same day as the Canada Section 338 deadline. The prior national CPI reading (released July 23) was 1.7% YoY national; Tokyo CPI ran 2.0% in July, suggesting the national print could approach or match the BOJ's 2% target. ING projected headline CPI at 2.0% YoY and core at 1.8% YoY for the August 21 release. Japan July trade statistics released August 20 are an additional data point. The structural backdrop is unchanged: BOJ at 1.0% vs Fed at 3.50-3.75%, wide but narrowing rate differential; yen short positioning remains elevated; JGB 10-year at 30-year highs per Trading Economics (August 18), adding fiscal pressure; Japan Q2 GDP was 0.5% QoQ in line with consensus (August 17), confirming above-potential growth.

implications.JPY: MAXIMUM tailwind from three converging forces: (1) G2 intervention with Bessent re-entry warning nominally active; (2) BOJ Sep hike probability now ~80% per MUFG, confirmed by Reuters sources; (3) Fed Sep hike odds ~39-40%, narrowing rate differential from both sides. Counter-risk: USDJPY at 158.50+ with no follow-up intervention for 17+ days allows carry rebuild. If 160 breaks on a daily close without official response, regime credibility damage will be severe. Japan CPI Aug 21 — at or above 2.0% YoY = cements Sep BOJ hike, JPY-supportive; sub-1.8% core = hike shifts to October, USDJPY lifts toward 160.
implications.USD: BOJ intervention chatter actively depressing broad DXY; USDJPY topside capped by intervention threat and growing BOJ hike pricing. Fed Sep hike odds ~39-40%, MUFG baseline sees hold. USDJPY most vulnerable into Japan CPI Aug 21, BOJ Sep 17-18, and Jackson Hole Aug 28.
implications.EUR: EUR/JPY sold by intervention mechanism. EUR/USD at ~1.1590 (2-month high) on combined BOJ intervention chatter and fading Fed hike expectations. ECB at 2.40% vs Fed at 3.75%.
implications.GBP: GBP/JPY under dual intervention and carry-unwind pressure. GBP/USD near 1.3560 (3-month highs). BoE cutting limits GBP outperformance vs EUR. Two-way risk into Jackson Hole.
implications.CHF: CHF/JPY lower on intervention pressure. USDCHF under pressure from broad USD softness. SNB in easing mode.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower; CAD FX dominated by Section 338 binary Aug 21 above all else. USD softness partially compresses USDCAD.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY under intervention pressure. AUDUSD on multi-week winning streak. Watch AUDJPY 93-95 range.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under intervention pressure; NZDUSD benefits from USD softness.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY 160.00 is the immediate critical level — a daily close above 160 without official verbal or actual intervention signals carry traders overpowering the regime and constitutes a credibility break. USDJPY below 157.50 = intervention credibility reasserting. USDJPY below 155.20 (post-intervention low Aug 3) = regime decisively winning. Japan national CPI Aug 21 — headline at or above 2.0% YoY = cements Sep BOJ hike (~80% already priced), JPY-supportive; sub-1.8% core = hike risk shifts to October, USDJPY lifts toward 160. Japan July trade statistics Aug 20 — deficit expansion = JPY headwind; surprise surplus = JPY supportive. BOJ Sep 17-18 meeting is the live hard binary: hike to 1.25% = fundamental JPY support materialises, reduces intervention burden significantly; no hike = JPY sells off sharply, 160+ re-test. Jackson Hole Aug 28 (Warsh keynote) — dovish USD framing extends JPY-positive environment; hawkish framing partially restores rate differential drag on JPY. Any MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately. JGB 10-year at 30-year highs — if approaches 3.0%, BOJ forced to defend bonds vs yen simultaneously, creating internal policy conflict.

themes.title: Warsh Fed — FOMC minutes Aug 19 released, Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 (7 days) is dominant USD binary, Sep hike odds ~39-40%, July PCE Aug 27 is pre-keynote risk
themes.summary: As of August 20, the Jackson Hole symposium is 7 days away and remains the dominant USD binary event on the macro calendar. The FOMC minutes from the July 28-29 meeting were released at 2:00pm ET on August 19. Newsquawk flagged pre-release that markets risked looking through the minutes given their backward-looking nature — particularly following the significant inflation and labour market data released since the July meeting — with attention likely to remain on Jackson Hole. The established pattern with three-dissent meetings (as July 29 produced) is that the count of officials who expressed sympathy with the dissenters matters more than the dissenters' own arguments. The July 29 FOMC vote was confirmed at 9-3 to hold at 3.50-3.75%. EUR/USD rose to a fresh 2-month high near 1.1590 in the run-up to the minutes, with GBP/USD near 3-month highs around 1.3560 — both dollar-driven advances reflecting the repricing of Fed hike expectations away from the hawkish late-July positioning. Jackson Hole runs August 27-29 under the theme 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy,' with roughly 120 central bankers from over 70 countries attending. Warsh delivers his first keynote as Federal Reserve Chair on Friday morning August 28 — 19 days before the September 16 FOMC decision, making it effectively the last major opportunity for the Fed to signal rate-path intent before the meeting. Under Warsh, the Fed no longer telegraphs its intentions ahead of meetings, meaning this speech carries genuine information value. Warsh told reporters on July 29 that his keynote is 'a blank piece of paper right now' and that remarks will focus on 'long-term structural questions, not near-term guidance' — but analysts note the Sep 16 FOMC proximity and data conflict (inflation at 3.4% vs 2% target, NFP -23K) means every clause will be traded. Kalkine notes that the 2026 theme sits at a greater distance from immediate rate-setting concerns than most recent years — the disconnect between the academic programme and market's rate-path focus is unusually wide, making the policy signal harder to read from the title alone. The data backdrop: July CPI +0.1% MoM / +3.4% YoY (August 12), July PPI flat 0.0% vs 0.2% consensus (August 14), NFP -23K vs +80K consensus (August 7) — all three pushing against a September hike. Sep hike odds ~39-40%. MUFG baseline sees Fed holding in September. Critical pre-keynote risk: July PCE releases August 27 — the morning Jackson Hole opens — creating a potential data/event cascade. Nvidia earnings August 26 evening place the market's largest single-stock event 36 hours before the biggest Fed event, with potential equity risk-on/risk-off spillover into FX around the JH open. Sep 11 CPI (August data) is the next major data event post-JH. Sep 16 FOMC is the hard policy event.

implications.USD: EUR/USD near 1.1590 (2-month high) and GBP/USD near 1.3560 (3-month high) reflect broad USD weakness from data miss trifecta and fading hike expectations. Jackson Hole Aug 28 is the primary binary: hawkish Warsh (Sep hike still on table) restores USD carry bid 100-150 pips across EUR/USD, GBP/USD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD; dovish or structural/framework speech extends USD weakness toward Q3 upper targets — EUR/USD retests 1.17+, DXY toward 98-99. FOMC minutes on Aug 19 were the immediate near-term catalyst; Newsquawk flagged risk markets look through them to JH. MUFG baseline now sees Fed holding in September.
implications.JPY: Rate differential headwind from Warsh narrative significantly reduced by NFP + CPI + PPI data miss trio. Dovish JH framing = USDJPY three-pillar bearish case (intervention + fading Fed + live BOJ hike) reinforced. Hawkish JH = rate differential widens modestly but intervention credibility still caps topside near 160.
implications.EUR: EUR/USD at ~1.1590 (2-month high), barrier at 1.1600. ECB at 2.40% vs Fed at 3.75%. Warsh dovish at JH = EUR/USD retests 1.17-1.19; hawkish = EUR/USD pulls back toward 1.1280. July PCE on Aug 27 (JH open day) is pre-keynote data risk. Nvidia-driven risk-on Aug 26 may amplify EUR bid into JH.
implications.GBP: GBP/USD near 3-month peaks at 1.3560 — two-way risk into JH. BoE cutting limits GBP outperformance vs EUR. JH keynote Aug 28 drives near-term direction.
implications.CAD: USD softness provides USDCAD compressing tailwind but Section 338 binary on Aug 21 supersedes this narrative entirely for USDCAD this week. Post-Aug 21 resolution, Fed theme reasserts.
implications.AUD: RBA on hold with easing bias. AUDUSD on multi-week winning streak, supported by USD softness. Watch 0.6500-0.6650 range into JH.
implications.NZD: RBNZ same dynamic as RBA. NZDUSD benefits from broad USD softness into JH.
implications.CHF: SNB in easing mode; USDCHF under pressure. CHF safe-haven bid in risk-off episodes around JH volatility.
